text: here is a question i have that could help or be a red herring, but, look at the staircase. what exactly is it? because, if i look at it, it looks like one big solid slant right. but thats not the case. i know this because for a long time we had t he problem where i could walk under the stairs through an invisible wall. So, that must mean, from what im thinking, is that there is a wall piece inside of the staircase, maybe causing the problem
resolution: Answered the user's hypothesis that a wall piece hidden inside the staircase causes the stick (recalling the old walk-under-the-stairs invisible-wall bug). The stairlog data rules a solid wall out: a solid-rect block would show a non-zero rectpush column (the side-push pulling the player off the desired path), but it reads (0.000,0.000) on every stuck frame, and hfcancel=false rules out the too-steep terrain move-cancel. The staircase collides as a heightfield slope (placedPieceRamps/registerStairSlope), not a wall piece, and the evidence points at the uphill speed-clamp misreading the crest cell rather than any collider. Added integ=()/clamp=() velocity instrumentation to confirm (commit 86f5f35c8); if integ is large while clamp is tiny, the speed-clamp is the cause.
